title: Which extra fact is sufficient to prove it?
subtitle: Lines, angles, and triangles · 12 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **12 of the official questions in Lines, angles, and triangles are this one** — 3 Easy, 3 Medium, 6 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question stem asks which additional information is sufficient to prove something: two lines are parallel, two triangles are similar, or two triangles are congruent.
- Some facts are already given, and each choice (or each of the Roman-numeral statements I/II/III) adds a condition.
- The answer is a condition, not a number.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) List what you already have, such as one pair of equal angles or two side lengths.
- 2) Name the criterion you need to finish.
- Parallel lines need corresponding or alternate interior angles equal, or same-side interior angles supplementary.
- Similarity needs AA, SAS~ (equal included angle and proportional sides), or SSS~.
- Congruence needs SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, or HL.
- 3) Test each option: does adding it complete the criterion?

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: This is a logic question about criteria, with nothing to graph or compute.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a condition that is true whenever the lines cross (vertical angles, a linear pair), so it can't prove parallelism.
For similarity you accept proportional sides when the equal angle isn't the one between them (SSA).
For congruence you accept angles alone (AAA), or a right angle without the hypotenuse-leg or side matching it needs.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You pick a condition that is true whenever the lines cross (vertical angles, a linear pair), so it can't prove parallelism.
For similarity you accept proportional sides when the equal angle isn't the one between them (SSA).
